- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) after a price spike, model often overshoots downward; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to avoid premature correction.
- Model frequently underestimates prices in the first 5–7 days of a new 30-day horizon, especially after strong recent highs; apply a 1–2% upward bias for early days.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model shows mean-reversion bias; align forecast with recent 7-day average if sentiment is weak.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 18-day high, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.80).
- If model forecast is <10% below recent 18-day low, increase by 5–10% unless sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.20).
- Sentiment spikes (e.g., 1.00) after a low price often trigger model overreaction; dampen forecast by 2–5% for 2–3 days post-spike.
- Model tends to lag sentiment shifts by 2–5 days; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change if sentiment is trending.
